slides.title: Why every day trader watches VWAP.
What VWAP is
slides.small: From the session open · price = (high + low + close) ÷ 3
slides.text: The **average price everyone paid today**, weighted by how much was traded at each price.

slides.title: Reclaim, retest, hold
slides.text: Price gets back above VWAP, comes back to test it, and buyers defend it. In this example **every close after the reclaim stays above**.

slides.title: Reading VWAP
slides.text: Above it, today's average buyer is in profit. Below it, today's average buyer is losing.

points.t: Intraday VWAP starts again at the open. Yesterday's line is a different thing.

points.b: It's a reference, not a wall
points.t: Price often chops around it before choosing a side.
A reclaim means more when it also breaks a level.

slides.title: VWAP tells you who's in control today.
slides.text: Watch the reclaim, then the retest. A hold is the confirmation.

post.instagram:
VWAP is the average price everyone paid today, weighted by volume, starting from the session open. Above it, today's average buyer is in profit; below it, the average buyer is losing. A reclaim followed by a retest that holds is one of the cleanest things to watch intraday.
